==English==
{{wp|<dab!>}}
{{commons|money}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|monie||archaic}}
* {{alter|en|mony||obsolete}}
* {{alter|en|munney|munny||eye dialect}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:moneye|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|moneye}}, {{m|enm|moneie}}, {{m|enm|money}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|muneie||money}}, from {{der|en|la|monēta||money, a place for coining money, coin, mint}}, from the name of the temple of Juno Moneta in Rome, where a mint was.

In this sense, displaced native {{ncog|ang|feoh}}, whence {{cog|en|fee}}. {{doublet|en|mint}}, ultimately from the same Latin word but through Germanic and Old English, and of {{m|en|manat}}, through Russian and Azerbaijani or Turkmen.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|a=RP|/ˈmʌn.i/}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-money.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|a=GA|/ˈmʌn.i/|[ˈmɐni]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-money.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmʊn.i/|a=Northern England}}
* {{IPA|en|a=Scotland|/ˈmʌn.e/}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌni|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|mon|ey}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|ies|s}} {{tlb|en|plural used only in certain senses}}
[[File:US-Colonial (PA-149)-Pennsylvania-20 Mar 1771 OBV.jpg|thumb|right|180px|[[w:Shilling|Twenty Shilling]] banknote issued by the [[w:Pennsylvania Colony|Pennysylvania Colony]] in 1771.]]

# {{senseid|en|Q1368}} A generally accepted means of [[exchange]].
#: {{ux|en|I cannot take '''money''' that I did not work for.}}
#: {{ux|en|Before colonial times cowry shells imported from Mauritius were used as '''money''' in Western Africa.}}
#: {{ux|en|How is she fixed for '''money'''? She used to spend '''money''' [[every day]] on makeup.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage=Then there came a reg'lar terror of a sou'wester same as you don't get one summer in a thousand, and blowed the shanty flat and ripped about half of the weir poles out of the sand. We spent consider'ble '''money''' getting 'em reset, and then a swordfish got into the pound and tore the nets all to slathers, right in the middle of the squiteague season.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21583277-worlds-biggest-polluter-going-green-it-needs-speed-up-transition-can-china Can China clean up fast enough?]
|passage=At the same time, it is pouring '''money''' into cleaning up the country.}}
# A [[currency]] maintained by a state or other entity which can guarantee its value (such as a monetary union). {{rfc-sense|en}}
#: {{ux|en|'''money''' supply;  '''money''' market}}
# {{senseid|en|Q693464}} [[hard cash#English:_banknotes and coins|Hard cash]] in the form of [[banknote]]s and [[coin]]s, as opposed to [[cheque#English:_Q80042|cheque]]s, [[credit card]]s, or [[credit]] more generally.
#: {{ux|en|You best have some '''money''', cause there ain't no [[check#English:_Q80042|checks]] or [[credit#English:_Q182076|credit]] here.}}
# The total value of [[liquid asset]]s available for an individual or other economic unit, such as cash and bank deposits.
# [[wealth|Wealth]].
#: {{ux|en|He was born with '''money'''.}}
# A person, family or class that possesses wealth.
#: {{ux|en|He was born into '''money'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|He married '''money'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Megan Nolan|title=‘I grew up on an “estate from hell” but I have no idea what class I am’: novelist Megan Nolan on the conundrum of identity|date=2023-07-15|url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2023/jul/15/i-grew-up-on-an-estate-from-hell-megan-nolan-on-class|passage= I grew up in Ballybeg, neither of my working-class parents came from '''money''' or went to university, so I was part of a working-class family, I assumed.}}
# An item of [[value]] between two or more parties used for the exchange of [[goods]] or [[services]].
# A person who funds an operation.
